extracted.intended_audience: high-school students training for mathematical olympiads (IMO/MOSP) and teachers/mentors preparing such students
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of trigonometry fundamentals, identities, geometric techniques, and problem-solving advice aimed at preparing students for olympiad-style trig problems and training programs (e.g., MOSP/IMO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Take your time
rubrics_metrics.description: Very few contestants can solve all the given problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to pace yourself during practice and contests; do not expect to solve every problem immediately or in one sitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make connections between problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to make connections between problems. An important theme of this work is that all important techniques and ideas featured in the book appear more than once!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When solving, look for recurring tactics/ ideas and reuse methods seen elsewhere; build a toolkit of techniques that apply to multiple problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be patient and try varied approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Olympiad problems don’t 'crack' immediately. Be patient. Try different approaches. Experiment with simple cases. In some cases, working backwards from the desired result is helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically try simplifications, special cases, constructions, substitutions, working backwards, and other heuristic approaches instead of expecting a single obvious trick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read solutions even if you solved the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you can solve a problem, do read the solutions. They may contain some ideas that did not occur in your solutions, and they may discuss strategic and tactical approaches that can be used elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided solutions as models of elegant presentation; attempt to reconstruct the thinking that led to them and identify key ideas and transferable methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisit problems and seek alternate solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Go back to the original problem later, and see whether you can solve it in a different way. Many of the problems have multiple solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use revisitation to deepen understanding, find more elegant or shorter approaches, and expand your repertoire of techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular practice and resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful problem-solving takes practice. Don’t get discouraged if you have trouble at first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persist through difficulties, use recommended reading for more practice, and treat problem-solving as a skill that improves with consistent effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-triangle (elementary) definitions of trig functions
rubrics_metrics.description: For an acute angle θ, define sin, cos, tan, cot, csc, sec from ratios in a right triangle; show these are well defined (independent of point choice) via similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similarity of right triangles to justify definitions and to derive basic relations; reduce many geometry problems to right-triangle trigonometry when convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-circle definition and periodicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Define sin θ and cos θ as the coordinates of the point on the unit circle at polar angle θ; extend trig functions to all angles and note periodicity (sin, cos period 360°; tan, cot period 180°).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use polar coordinates and unit circle symmetries to derive identities like sin(θ±180°) = −sin θ, sin(90°−θ)=cos θ, and to reason about periodicity and sign changes across quadrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic reciprocal and Pythagorean identities
rubrics_metrics.description: sin2 A + cos2 A = 1; tan = sin/cos, cot = cos/sin; csc, sec reciprocals; derived identities 1 + cot2 = csc2, 1 + tan2 = sec2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are foundational algebraic tools for transforming expressions, simplifying, and checking results; used pervasively in problem solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-angle exact values
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact trigonometric values for 30°, 45°, 60° (e.g., sin45° = cos45° = √2/2; sin30° = 1/2, cos60° = 1/2; sin60° = √3/2, tan60° = √3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use known exact values to simplify and test expressions; construct or recall standard geometric derivations (equilateral/isosceles right triangles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition and subtraction formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: sin(α±β) = sinα cosβ ± cosα sinβ; cos(α±β) = cosα cosβ ∓ sinα sinβ; tan(α±β) = (tanα ± tanβ)/(1 ∓ tanα tanβ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived geometrically (e.g., rectangle/inscribed right-triangle constructions) and valid for all angles; central for combining angles and deriving many other identities (double/triple-angle, sum-to-product, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-angle, triple-angle, and half-angle formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-angle: sin2α = 2 sinα cosα, cos2α = cos2α − sin2α = 1 − 2 sin2α, tan2α = 2 tanα/(1−tan2α). Triple-angle and half-angle formulas are special cases derived from addition/subtraction formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to reduce multi-angle expressions, derive half-angle substitutions, and transform between trig functions and algebraic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum-to-product and product-to-sum formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: sin a + sin b = 2 sin((a+b)/2) cos((a−b)/2); 2 sin a cos b = sin(a+b)+sin(a−b), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for converting sums into products (and vice versa), simplifying integrals/series-like expressions, and in many olympiad manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sinusoidal function representation and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: A sinusoidal function has form y = a sin[b(x + c)] + d; a is amplitude, b relates to period, c horizontal shift, d vertical shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form to analyze and sketch trig graphs, combine sinusoids (linear combinations with same period remain sinusoidal), and understand Fourier-like decompositions in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphs of tangent/cotangent and discontinuities
rubrics_metrics.description: y = tan x and y = cot x are not continuous; tan x has vertical asymptotes at x = (2k+1)·90°, cot x at x = k·180°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep domain restrictions in mind when manipulating expressions and solving equations; consider asymptotic behavior in inequalities and limit problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area formulas involving trig
rubrics_metrics.description: Area of triangle ABC: [ABC] = (1/2)ab sin C (equivalently 1/2 bc sin A = 1/2 ca sin B); generalizations for quadrilaterals via diagonal products and sine of included angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply area formula to convert between lengths and angles, compute areas efficiently, and derive relations (e.g., in trapezoid examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of Sines and Extended Law of Sines
rubrics_metrics.description: sin A / a = sin B / b = sin C / c, hence a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R where R is circumradius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to relate sides and angles, compute circumradius, prove angle-bisector theorem, and solve non-right triangles in contest problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle-bisector theorem (via law of sines)
rubrics_metrics.description: If AD is an internal angle bisector in triangle ABC meeting BC at D, then AB/AC = BD/CD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive from law of sines in subtriangles ABD and ACD; helpful in many geometry/trig ratio problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceva’s theorem (and trigonometric form)
rubrics_metrics.description: For cevians AD, BE, CF of triangle ABC, concurrency is equivalent to (AF/FB)·(BD/DC)·(CE/EA) = 1. Trigonometric form: product of appropriate side ratios or product of sin(angle ratios) = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test or enforce concurrency of cevians, both in pure length form and trig form involving sines of adjacent angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jensen’s inequality and convexity/concavity for trig sums
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is convex, f(λ1x1+...+λnxn) ≤ λ1f(x1)+...+λnf(xn); applied to trig (e.g., sin is concave on [0,π], tan is convex on [0,π/2)), giving inequalities such as sinA+sinB+sinC ≤ 3√3/2 for triangle angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to obtain bounds on sums of trig functions over angle sets; apply when function curvature (second derivative) is known or when weighted averages appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of Cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: In triangle ABC: |CA|^2 = |AB|^2 + |BC|^2 − 2|AB|·|BC| cos ∠ABC (and analogous cyclic forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to generalize Pythagorean relations, compute sides/angles in non-right triangles, and in algebraic manipulations involving cosines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewart’s Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: For triangle ABC with cevian AD, writing a=BC, b=CA, c=AB, m=BD, n=DC, d=AD, then d^2 a + m a n = c^2 n + b^2 m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to compute lengths of cevians (medians, angle bisectors, altitudes in some cases) in terms of side lengths; helpful in length-chasing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heron’s formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Area of triangle with sides a,b,c: [ABC] = sqrt(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)) where s=(a+b+c)/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compute area from side lengths when angles are not directly available or to convert between side-based and angle-based formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: (Σ ai^2)(Σ bi^2) ≥ (Σ aibi)^2 with equality iff vectors are proportional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply in algebraic/trig inequalities to bound sums/products, and to convert geometric dot-product relations into inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Moivre’s formula
rubrics_metrics.description: (cos α + i sin α)^n = cos nα + i sin nα for integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with complex numbers to expand cos(nα) and sin(nα) in terms of cosα and sinα, derive multiple-angle expansions, and handle trigonometric polynomial manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler’s formula in plane geometry (OI^2 relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For triangle circumcenter O, incenter I with circumradius R and inradius r: |OI|^2 = R^2 − 2rR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specialized geometric identity connecting incenter and circumcenter useful in advanced triangle-geometry problems involving radii and centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigonometric identities compendium (reference list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of many standard identities: sin^2+cos^2=1, addition/subtraction formulas, double/triple/half-angle formulas, sum-to-product, product-to-sum, expansion formulas for sin nα and cos nα, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compendium as a quick reference during problem solving; many contest solutions rely on selecting and composing several of these identities.
